newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, yen bounces in ranges.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, yen bounces in ranges.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed, as yen contracts bounced around in narrow ranges ahead of Japan's May trade surplus data, currency traders and analysts said.
"It's difficult to take an aggressive long dollar position ahead of that number," Bob Lynch, currency strategist at Paribas Capital Markets, said.

The lack of direction in the dollar translated into a September yen that flitted between marginal gains and losses for most of the session. September caught buy-top orders, but failed to test Monday's session high of $0.008957.

Lynch said the market is bracing for a sharp increase in Japan's May trade surplus. The data will be released at 1950 EDT/2350 GMT while currency futures are trading on GLOBEX. A Reuters poll is predicting Japan's trade surplus will widen to 548.5 billion yen from 229 billion yen in April.

However, Lynch said Japanese officials have been effective in the last week or so of talking the dollar slightly higher. He expects dollar/yen to trade between 112.00 and 115.00 spot in the near term, which equals $0.009044 and $0.008811 in September yen.
U.S. international trade numbers will be released on Thursday. The U.S. is expected to post a deficit of $10 billion in April, up from $8.5 billion in March.
Trade issues are expected to be discussed at the Group of Seven's (G7) summit in Denver on June 20-22.

U.S. Treasury assistant secretary David Lipton told reporters on Tuesday that the G7 is expected to back a broad commitment to promote sustainable economic growth and avoid excessive trade imbalances.
Lipton said President Clinton is expected to discuss the need for Japan to maintain strong domestic demand-led growth and avoid an unhealthy rise in its trade surplus.

September yen started to set fresh intraday highs on the comments, but trade was extremely light. Several traders and analysts noted that Lipton's comments reiterated recent statements from various U.S. Treasury officials.
Earlier in the day September yen fell to a session low of $0.008911, near support at $0.008904, in reaction to U.S. May industrial producation and capacity utilization data.
Production rose 0.4 percent and use increased to 83.7 percent, versus forecasts for up 0.2 percent and unchanged, respectively.

September marks also reacted negatively to the data, given the absence of details on the EMU stability pact, traders said. September inched towards the GLOBEX low of $0.5791. Major support rests at the contract low of $0.5770.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was up $0.000005 at $0.008937, marks were down $0.0004 at $0.5809, Swiss francs fell $0.0020 at $0.6991, sterling was up $0.0028 at $1.6356, Canadian dollars were $0.0002 higher at $0.7250, Australian dollars were $0.0019 higher at $0.7516 and Mexican pesos were $0.000325 higher at $0.121450.
